title: POC hybrid routing & precision profile notes
content:
Purpose:
This is the working record from the 2025-11-03 workshop + follow-ups for the customer POC (enterprise search + summarization). Focus: choosing model variants and precision profiles, routing/fallback rules, and prompt + pipeline tuning for best tradeoff across latency/cost/quality.

Context / customer constraints:
- Customer: FinaTrust (regulated fintech). PII-containing documents, strict internal SLAs: p95 latency <= 800ms for single-turn query, and end-to-end summarization pipeline (retrieval + generation) <= 2.2s.
- Throughput target: burst to 200 qps during peak trading hours; steady ~30 qps otherwise.
- Security: private deployment (VPC) with KMS; logs redaction required, KV cache must be transient and tenant-scoped.
- Quality bar: abstractive summary should preserve numerical fidelity and not hallucinate critical fields; target human eval pass >= 90% on sample set.

Workshop notes (high level):
- Goal: identify 2 candidate model families and 3 operational profiles (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized) to run in dedicated capacity for a 6-week POC.
- Tradeoffs discussed: quantization-induced quality drift vs cost savings; routing based on request priority and length; prefix cache reuse for repeated queries.
- Whiteboard decisions: prefer hybrid routing (fast path -> smaller quantized model; slow path -> fp16 or q4f16 larger model).

Model candidates considered and rationale:
1) Mistral-7B-like (LLaMA-derivative family) 7B baseline
   - Why: strong instruction following, smaller KV cache size, cheap tokens, good for short answers and high QPS.
   - Risk: may struggle on long-document faithful summarization without retrieval prompt engineering.
2) Falcon-40B-ish medium variant (32-40B)
   - Why: higher factuality on longer contexts, strong summarization quality out of the box.
   - Risk: higher memory and latency; more expensive to run at scale.
3) Claude-style open model (best-in-class long-context)
   - Why: outperforms on multi-document coherence in initial evals.
   - Risk: heavier, more operational complexity.

Precision/quantization profiles evaluated:
- fp16 (baseline for quality): highest fidelity, highest cost. Use for slow path and final-rendering stage.
- q4f16 / q4_0 (4-bit float/fp16 hybrid): good quality/cost balance on many decoder models; tested as main candidate for balanced profile.
- 8-bit int (int8 / nf4): lower memory than fp16 but sometimes introduces numerical instability with certain beam lengths; good for low-latency path if confirmed by evals.
- 3-bit / extreme quant (experimental): only for cacheable deterministic reranking where hallucination is low risk.

Key experiments run (summary of results):
- Setup: Dedicated nodes (A100 equivalent), same prompt templates. Bench benchmark harness with synthetic query mix (mix replicates: 60% short Q/A, 25% retrieval summarization, 15% long-form explainers). Metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), token-cost estimate, and human QA pass rate (50-shot sampled).
- Experiment A: 7B q4f16 (balanced) as single model
   - p50: 65ms, p95: 210ms (generation only), throughput: 380 qps (short), cost: 0.22 USD per 1k tokens (est), human QA pass: 78% (on abstractive numeric fidelity tests).
- Experiment B: 40B q4f16 (balanced large)
   - p50: 210ms, p95: 620ms, throughput: 95 qps, cost: 1.1 USD per 1k tokens, human QA pass: 92%.
- Experiment C: hybrid routing (7B q4f16 fast path + 40B fp16 slow path) with routing by query type + confidence score
   - Routing policy: length > 1,200 tokens OR retrieval_count > 3 OR prompt includes financial-numeric tag => route to slow path; else fast path. Also fallback to slow on low-confidence / hallucination risk heuristics.
   - Observed system: effective p50 overall = 95ms, p95 = 480ms, effective throughput 130 qps steady, cost reduced ~45% vs always-40B. Human QA pass (after merging outputs with final fp16 post-check for flagged items) = 90.5%.
- Experiment D: 40B q4f16 (quantized large)
   - p50: 180ms, p95: 540ms, throughput: 110 qps, cost: 0.6 USD per 1k tokens, human QA pass: 89% (small drop vs fp16 on edge numeric cases).

Notes on KV/prefix caching and batching:
- Prefix reuse: customer query patterns have high repeated prefixes for instrument tickers; KV caching reduces generation latency by ~20% on fast path when warm.
- Cache TTL: set to 10 minutes for tenant-scoped entries; eviction policy LRU with capacity per-tenant hard limit.
- Batching: continuous batching helped throughput for short Qs; batch size cap for fast path = 16, for slow path = 4 to keep latency SLOs.

Prompt/pipeline tuning (key takeaways):
- Retrieval augmentation: structured retrieval (table-aware retrieval) + template that instructs model to "copy numeric fields verbatim" dramatically reduces hallucination. Add a trailing verification prompt that extracts numbers and validates with source IDs.
- Reranking: small 1B re-ranker (dense embeddings + cross-encoder quick check) before generation improved final quality by ~6% absolute on our QA metric with ~30ms overhead.
- Two-stage generation pattern: draft with fast 7B, then if draft flagged by numeric-checker, regenerate on 40B fp16 with the original context + discrepancy hints. This pattern reduces average cost while keeping final QA high.

Operational profiles (recommended):
1) Low-latency (fast path heavy): 7B q4f16 on dedicated pool, batching aggressive, KV warm; reserve burst V100 GPUs for spiky loads. Use for low-priority non-numeric answers.
2) Balanced (default POC profile): hybrid routing: 7B q4f16 + 40B q4f16 plus fp16 fallback for flagged items; moderate batching, prefix cache enabled.
3) High-fidelity (regulatory): 40B fp16 primary; q4f16 allowed for background summarization but all numeric-sensitive outputs re-run on fp16.

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- Edge-case numeric regressions in q4f16 for 40B family: need 200 additional numeric QA samples.
- Cold cache behaviour during peak bursts: measure warm-up time and effect on p95.
- KMS/HSM integration with private nodes: ensure key rotation does not interrupt model weights loading.
- Legal: requirement about summary retention window (customer asks for 90-day retention; need to confirm with security/compliance).

Action items and owners:
- Marcus: run expanded numeric QA sweep (200 cases) across q4f16 vs fp16 for 40B by 2026-03-20.
- Priya: prototype the two-stage draft+verify pipeline and integrate the numeric-checker (conservative) into the routing logic — due 2026-03-15.
- Evan: load-test cold-cache ramp for hybrid cluster to reproduce p95 variability — due 2026-03-12.
- Sofia: confirm tenant-scoped KV encryption and KMS key rotation behaviour with security team — due 2026-03-14.
- Lena: create customer-facing one-pager summarizing recommended profile and estimated costs — due 2026-03-11.

Appendix: quick heuristics for routing classifier (draft)
- If query contains token patterns matching regex (\b(balance|balance-sheet|net-income|PNL|USD\b)) or looks like a numeric-heavy request => score +2.
- If retrieval returns > 2 doc IDs with table metadata => score +1.
- If 7B draft passes numeric-checker => final (no slow path). Else route to slow path.

Meeting log (selected timestamps):
- 2025-11-03 09:10 Workshop kick-off (intro, constraints)
- 2025-11-03 09:45 Whiteboard: routing policies, edge cases
- 2025-11-03 11:00 Initial bench run kickoff (A/B experiments)
- 2025-11-10 10:30 Follow-up: added q4f16 large runs, discussed results

Status summary:
- Current recommended default for POC: Balanced hybrid routing with q4f16 on both sizes and fp16 fallback for flagged numeric outputs. This meets p95 target in most traffic mixes and hits QA pass ~90%.
- Next milestone: complete numeric QA sweep and cold-cache load tests, then finalize configuration for customer acceptance test (CAT).

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Try training a lightweight numeric verifier model that can run as an edge microservice to avoid expensive full fp16 re-runs for minor discrepancies.
- Explore per-tenant quantization profiles: some tenants may accept more aggressive quant for cost savings.

End of doc.
